outputs.L1: Representative embodiments are disclosed for a spinal disc device implantable between adjacent vertebral bodies. In one representative embodiment, the spinal disc device comprises: a first transverse plate member; a first arcuate extension extending longitudinally from the first transverse plate member and having a first configuration; a second transverse plate member; and a second arcuate extension extending longitudinally from the second transverse plate member and having a second configuration that mates with the first configuration of the first arcuate extension and is slideably movable relative to the first arcuate extension. The first and second arcuate extensions are further arranged to define a central through-channel between the first and second transverse plate members for holding bone graft material. In various embodiments, the first and second configurations of the first and second arcuate extensions each comprise a partially spherical, convex shell configuration that provides movement in both the sagittal and coronal planes for deformity correction.
outputs.L2: Example embodiments describe a spinal disc implant designed for placement between neighboring vertebral bodies. In one example, the spinal disc device includes a first transverse plate element, along with a first curved extension that projects longitudinally from that plate and has a first shape. The device also includes a second transverse plate element and a second curved extension extending longitudinally from the second plate. The second extension has a shape that mates with the shape of the first extension and is able to slide relative to it. The two curved extensions are also positioned so that, between the first and second transverse plate elements, they define a central passage extending through the device for receiving bone graft material. In certain embodiments, the respective shapes of the first and second curved extensions are each formed as partially spherical, convex shell structures, allowing motion in both the sagittal and coronal planes to assist in correcting deformities.
outputs.L3:
The spinal disc device is designed for implantation between adjacent vertebral bodies, where it functions as an interbody support structure. Once positioned in the disc space, the device helps maintain or restore the desired spacing between the vertebrae while providing a stable environment for fusion or other therapeutic objectives.

The device includes a first transverse plate member and a second transverse plate member. Each plate member is configured to engage a respective vertebral body, and each includes a corresponding arcuate extension. These arcuate extensions project from the plate members toward one another and are shaped to cooperate with each other when the device is assembled or implanted.

The arcuate extensions have complementary mating configurations. This allows the extensions to fit together while remaining slideably movable relative to one another. As a result, the first and second plate members can shift or articulate in a controlled manner, permitting adjustment of the device after placement or during correction of spinal alignment.

Together, the arcuate extensions define a central through-channel extending between the first and second transverse plate members. This channel is configured to receive and retain bone graft material or other osteogenic material. By holding the graft material within the device, the through-channel promotes bone growth between the adjacent vertebral bodies and may facilitate fusion over time.

In some embodiments, the arcuate extensions are formed as partially spherical convex shell structures. These shell-shaped extensions permit relative movement of the plate members in both the sagittal and coronal planes. This capability allows the device to accommodate or assist in correction of spinal deformities, including angular misalignment between adjacent vertebrae, while maintaining support and promoting fusion across the treated disc space.
outputs.L4:
A spinal disc device is provided for implantation in the intervertebral space between two adjacent vertebral bodies. The device is designed to restore or maintain disc height, assist in correcting spinal deformity, and promote fusion between the vertebrae after implantation.

The device includes a first transverse plate member and a second transverse plate member positioned generally opposite one another. Each plate member is configured to engage a respective vertebral endplate. The plate members include mating arcuate extensions that are slidably movable relative to one another. These arcuate extensions cooperate to define a central through-channel extending through the device. The through-channel is sized and shaped to receive bone graft material, bone substitute, or another osteogenic material, allowing bone growth through the implant and between the adjacent vertebral bodies.

The arcuate extensions of the plate members have partially spherical convex shell configurations. Because of this geometry, the plate members can move relative to one another while maintaining supportive contact. The sliding, curved interface permits controlled angular adjustment of the device in multiple directions, including movement in the sagittal plane and movement in the coronal plane. As a result, the implant can accommodate or assist in correction of spinal alignment, such as lordotic, kyphotic, or lateral deformities, depending on the orientation and positioning of the device.

When implanted, the device provides mechanical support between the adjacent vertebrae while leaving the central channel available for fusion material. The opposing plate members bear against the vertebral bodies and help maintain the desired spacing and alignment during the fusion process. The ability of the arcuate extensions to move relative to one another allows the implant to be adjusted to a desired angular relationship, thereby improving conformity to the patient’s anatomy and permitting correction of deformity before fusion is completed.

In use, the intervertebral disc space is prepared by removing at least a portion of the natural disc material and preparing the vertebral endplates. The device is then inserted into the disc space, with the first and second plate members positioned against the opposing vertebral bodies. Bone graft material may be placed within the central through-channel before, during, or after insertion. Once positioned, the device supports the vertebral bodies in the desired orientation while the graft material promotes bone growth through the channel, ultimately leading to fusion of the adjacent vertebrae.

Thus, the spinal disc device combines structural support, multi-planar adjustability, and a central fusion pathway. Its partially spherical, mating arcuate shell surfaces allow relative movement in both sagittal and coronal planes, enabling controlled deformity correction while maintaining a stable environment for spinal fusion.

**Representative**

A representative is a person chosen or appointed to speak, act, or make decisions on behalf of others. Representatives play an important role in many areas of society, including government, business, education, and community organizations. Their main responsibility is to understand the needs, opinions, and interests of the people they represent and to communicate those views clearly and fairly.

In politics, a representative is elected by citizens to participate in decision-making and create laws. This system allows people to have a voice in government without every individual being directly involved in every decision. A good political representative listens to the public, respects different opinions, and works to improve the community.

In business, a representative may speak for a company, promote products, support customers, or negotiate agreements. Sales representatives, customer service representatives, and company representatives all help build trust between an organization and the people it serves.

Being a representative requires responsibility, honesty, communication skills, and leadership. A representative should not act only in personal interest but should consider the goals and concerns of the group. Whether in government, business, or everyday life, representatives help connect people, share ideas, and make cooperation possible.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an implantable spinal disc device with two transverse plates, mating arcuate extensions, a central channel for bone graft, and partially spherical sliding shells allowing sagittal and coronal correction.
counterfactuals.output: An implantable spinal disc device is provided for placement between adjacent vertebral bodies. The device includes first and second transverse plates configured to engage opposing vertebral endplates, each plate having at least one arcuate extension arranged to mate with a corresponding arcuate extension of the other plate. The mating arcuate extensions define a guided interface and cooperate to form a central channel extending through the device for receiving bone graft material or other osteogenic media to promote interbody fusion. Partially spherical sliding shells are disposed between or along the plates and are configured to permit controlled relative angular movement of the plates, thereby enabling correction in both sagittal and coronal planes while maintaining vertebral spacing and load support. The arcuate extensions and sliding shells provide constrained articulation, alignment adjustment, and stabilization during implantation and fusion.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a representative embodiment description for a spinal interbody fusion device placed between adjacent vertebral bodies, emphasizing slideably mating arcuate extensions and a through-channel for bone graft material.
counterfactuals.output:
In one representative embodiment, a spinal interbody fusion device is configured for placement in an intervertebral disc space between adjacent vertebral bodies. The device includes a first body portion and a second body portion that cooperate to define an implant having a generally annular, oval, kidney-shaped, or other anatomically suitable footprint for supporting the adjacent vertebral endplates.

The first body portion includes a first arcuate extension projecting generally circumferentially from a base region of the first body portion. The second body portion includes a second arcuate extension projecting generally circumferentially from a base region of the second body portion. The first and second arcuate extensions are configured to slideably mate with one another such that the first body portion and the second body portion may be advanced relative to each other along a curved or arcuate path. In one embodiment, the arcuate extensions include complementary guide surfaces, rails, grooves, dovetail features, tongues, channels, or other interengaging structures that maintain alignment of the body portions during relative sliding movement.

The slideable mating relationship of the arcuate extensions permits the implant to be assembled, expanded, contracted, or otherwise adjusted within or prior to insertion into the intervertebral space. For example, the first and second body portions may be introduced in a reduced-profile configuration and then moved relative to one another along the arcuate interface to form a larger support structure once positioned between the adjacent vertebral bodies. The arcuate configuration may facilitate placement through an anterior, posterior, lateral, transforaminal, or oblique surgical approach while allowing the device to conform generally to the natural contour of the disc space.

The assembled device defines a through-channel extending between an upper surface configured to face a first vertebral body and a lower surface configured to face a second vertebral body. The through-channel is sized and shaped to receive bone graft material, bone substitute material, demineralized bone matrix, autograft, allograft, biologic material, or combinations thereof. In use, bone graft material disposed within the through-channel promotes bone growth through the device between the adjacent vertebral bodies to facilitate fusion.

The upper and lower surfaces of the device may include teeth, ridges, serrations, keels, roughened areas, porous regions, or other anti-migration features configured to engage the vertebral endplates and resist displacement after implantation. The device may further include one or more openings communicating with the through-channel to permit packing of graft material, vascular ingrowth, or visualization of graft placement. In some embodiments, the first and second body portions lock together after sliding engagement by a detent, ratchet, interference fit, threaded member, pin, clip, or other locking mechanism to maintain the selected configuration within the disc space.

The device may be formed from any suitable biocompatible material, including titanium, titanium alloy, stainless steel, cobalt-chromium alloy, polyetheretherketone (PEEK), carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer, ceramic, bioresorbable material, porous metal, or combinations thereof. The first and second body portions may be manufactured separately and assembled before implantation, or may be assembled in situ by slideably engaging the arcuate extensions within the intervertebral space.

In use, disc material is removed from between adjacent vertebral bodies to create a prepared intervertebral space. Bone graft material may be placed into the through-channel before or after insertion of the device. The first and second body portions are positioned such that their arcuate extensions slideably mate and cooperate to form the interbody fusion device. Once seated between the vertebral bodies, the device provides structural support to maintain disc height and alignment while the graft material in the through-channel promotes bony fusion across the intervertebral space.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise patent disclosure summary for a spinal disc implant comprising first and second plate members with convex arcuate extensions that mate and permit multidirectional movement.
counterfactuals.output:
A spinal disc implant is disclosed for replacement or supplementation of an intervertebral disc. The implant includes a first plate member configured for engagement with a first vertebral body and a second plate member configured for engagement with an adjacent second vertebral body. Each plate member includes a vertebral bearing surface and an opposing articulating surface. The articulating surfaces include complementary convex arcuate extensions and corresponding receiving regions that mate with one another to define an articulation interface.

The mating arcuate extensions permit controlled multidirectional relative movement between the first and second plate members, including flexion-extension, lateral bending, rotation, and combinations thereof, while maintaining the plate members in operative alignment. The arcuate geometry may provide a defined range of motion and may resist excessive translation or dislocation. The vertebral bearing surfaces may include fixation features, surface texturing, coatings, keels, teeth, spikes, openings, or porous regions to promote secure attachment and/or bone ingrowth.

In use, the implant is positioned between adjacent vertebrae after disc space preparation, with the first and second plate members seated against respective vertebral endplates. The interlocking convex arcuate extensions articulate to mimic natural spinal disc motion while preserving disc height and spinal stability.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, an expandable spinal disc replacement device having opposing transverse members, longitudinal arcuate shell extensions, and a central bone graft passage.
counterfactuals.output:
An expandable spinal disc replacement device is provided for implantation within an intervertebral disc space between adjacent vertebral bodies. The device includes a first end portion and an opposing second end portion arranged along a longitudinal axis of the device, the first and second end portions being configured to engage respective vertebral endplates. The device further includes a pair of opposing transverse members extending generally laterally between opposed side regions of the device, the transverse members defining at least a portion of a structural frame adapted to support compressive spinal loading.

A plurality of longitudinal arcuate shell extensions extend between the opposing transverse members. The longitudinal arcuate shell extensions are curved about at least a portion of the longitudinal axis and define an outer profile configured to conform generally to the intervertebral disc space. The arcuate shell extensions may be circumferentially spaced from one another so as to provide a cage-like body having open side regions for facilitating visualization, bone ingrowth, or graft incorporation. In certain embodiments, the arcuate shell extensions are resiliently or mechanically displaceable relative to one another to permit expansion of the device from a reduced insertion configuration to an expanded implanted configuration.

The opposing transverse members and the longitudinal arcuate shell extensions collectively define a central bone graft passage extending through the device. The central bone graft passage is dimensioned to receive bone graft material, bone substitute material, biologic material, or combinations thereof. The passage provides a continuous graft-receiving channel through the implant to promote fusion between the adjacent vertebral bodies following implantation.

The device may include an expansion mechanism operatively coupled to one or more of the opposing transverse members and the longitudinal arcuate shell extensions. The expansion mechanism may be configured to increase a height, width, lordotic angle, or combinations thereof of the device after placement within the intervertebral disc space. The expansion mechanism may include threaded members, wedges, cams, ratchets, linkages, elastically biased components, or other actuating structures suitable for selectively urging the transverse members apart or altering the spatial relationship of the shell extensions.

In use, the expandable spinal disc replacement device is introduced into the disc space in the reduced configuration. After positioning, the device is expanded to restore or maintain disc height and to provide stable engagement with the vertebral endplates. Bone graft material may be introduced into or through the central bone graft passage before, during, or after expansion. The opposing transverse members provide load-bearing support, while the longitudinal arcuate shell extensions define a supportive peripheral structure and maintain the central bone graft passage in communication with the adjacent vertebral bodies.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a patent abstract for a vertebral implant device where two partially spherical shell components slide relative to each other to enable deformity correction in sagittal and coronal planes.
counterfactuals.output: A vertebral implant device includes first and second partially spherical shell components configured for mutual sliding articulation. The shell components define complementary curved bearing surfaces that permit controlled relative movement between adjacent vertebral structures to enable correction of spinal deformity in both sagittal and coronal planes. The implant may be positioned between vertebral bodies or within a prepared spinal space and adjusted intraoperatively so that sliding displacement of the shell components changes angular orientation and/or height of the implant to restore desired spinal alignment. The partially spherical geometry provides multi-planar correction while maintaining surface contact and load distribution between the components. In some embodiments, the implant includes fixation features, locking elements, surface texturing, or bone-engaging structures to secure the corrected position after adjustment. The device thereby provides a compact articulating vertebral implant for controlled three-dimensional spinal alignment correction and stabilization.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
